prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1009; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- Records show the same major damage from an earlier, unreported accident; it is now claimed as new.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to an intersection in Pearland, Texas, where Driver 1 was turning left and was struck by Driver 2. Driver 1 reported neck pain and said the impact felt like a whiplash injury. The reported injury fits the type and force of this crash. Driver 2 and two independent witnesses gave accounts that match Driver 1's description of how the collision happened, and scene photographs support those accounts. Passenger was in Driver 1's vehicle at the time, as confirmed by witnesses and by officers at the scene. Most of the vehicle damage lines up with the impact described. However, a review of prior records shows the same major damage to the same areas from an earlier incident that was never reported to police or an insurer, and that damage is now being presented as part of this collision. Driver 1 is a named driver on the policy. Further review of the earlier records is recommended before the damage is assessed.
